How do Istanbul's Merter, Laleli, Osmanbey and Zeytinburnu wholesale hubs differ from Bursa mills?

Istanbul's four textile districts focus on finished garments, ready-stock wholesale, and cut-and-sew production: Merter leads in casualwear, jersey, and denim; Osmanbey specializes in mid-to-upper womenswear and eveningwear; Laleli serves export ready-stock; and Zeytinburnu concentrates on leather, knitwear, and fabric trade. Bursa focuses upstream on woven fabric, upholstery, shirting, and technical textiles inside organized industrial zones.

Türkiye remains Europe's largest textile producer, supported by export bodies including the [Istanbul Apparel Exporters' Association (İHKİB)](https://www.ihkib.org.tr/en/about-us/about-us)—which also organizes [IFCO Istanbul Fashion Connection](https://www.ihkib.org.tr/en/our-activities/ifco)—and Bursa's [Uludağ Textile Exporters' Association (UTİB)](https://uib.org.tr/en/associations-uludag-textile-exporters-association) alongside the [Uludağ Apparel and Clothing Exporters' Association (UHKİB)](https://uib.org.tr/en/associations-uludag-apparel-and-clothing-exporters-association). Under the [EU–Türkiye Customs Union](https://trade.ec.europa.eu/access-to-markets/en/content/eu-turkiye-customs-union), qualifying industrial goods move tariff-free into the EU, giving European brands shorter replenishment lead times than East Asia.

body.text: What MOQs (minimum order quantities) do Turkish apparel factories accept in 2026?

In 2026, direct Turkish cut-and-sew workshops in Istanbul typically accept 150 to 300 pieces per style and color for knitwear or jersey using stock fabric, rising to 500 to 1,000 pieces for custom-dyed fabrics or complex tailoring. Vertically integrated Bursa mills usually require 1,000 to 3,000 meters per custom weave or dye lot.

Because Türkiye's export sector—tracked nationally by the [Türkiye Exporters Assembly (TİM)](https://www.tim.org.tr/en/turkiyes-may-exports-reached-usd-225-billion)—competes on speed and mid-sized runs rather than ultra-low-cost mass volume, suppliers price small runs sharply higher if you demand custom Pantone dyeing or bespoke trims. Brands launching capsule collections can lower MOQs by selecting in-stock greige or dyed fabrics from Merter or Bursa stockists and focusing customization on fit, wash, and private-label trim.
How do you separate direct factories from trading middlemen?

You separate direct factories from trading middlemen by inspecting the cutting, sewing, and finishing floor in person, verifying the company's Turkish Chamber of Industry registration and export history, and confirming that the entity issuing your proforma invoice owns the production facility rather than subcontracting blindly.

Showrooms in Merter and Osmanbey frequently operate as sales offices for factories located in Bağcılar, Güngören, Esenyurt, or Anatolian cities, which is normal when disclosed transparently. Problems start when an undisclosed broker marks up pricing and hides quality control. Use this verification checklist during site visits:

items: Walk the production floor: Confirm cutting tables, sewing lines, ironing, and quality-control stations match the quoted capacity.
Check legal identity: Match the company name on the tax plate (vergi levhası) with the business card and proforma invoice.
Verify exporter membership: Ask whether the supplier is registered with İHKİB, UTİB, or UHKİB and handles direct export invoices.
Inspect sample room ownership: Direct manufacturers normally employ in-house pattern makers (modelist) who can adjust tech packs on site.
Review compliance audits: Request current social or environmental audit certificates directly from the issuing body if required by your retail market.

faq.q: Can I visit both Istanbul apparel districts and Bursa fabric mills in 3 days?
faq.a: Yes. Two days in Istanbul (grouping Merter/Zeytinburnu and Osmanbey/Bağcılar) plus one dedicated day in Bursa via the Osmangazi Bridge allows 6 to 9 substantive appointments without losing hours to cross-city traffic.

faq.q: Do Merter and Osmanbey showrooms sell to small international brands?
faq.a: Yes. Many Merter and Osmanbey suppliers offer ready-stock wholesale with low minimums (sometimes 1 to 3 size series per style) alongside private-label manufacturing starting around 150 to 300 pieces per style.

faq.q: Do I need an interpreter when visiting Turkish textile factories?
faq.a: Export managers at larger Bursa mills and major Istanbul exporters often speak English, but pattern makers, floor supervisors, and mid-sized workshops usually work in Turkish. Bringing an independent interpreter prevents costly spec misunderstandings.

faq.q: How long does sampling take in Istanbul and Bursa?
faq.a: If stock fabric is available locally, initial prototype samples typically take 7 to 14 days. Custom-woven or custom-dyed fabric development from a Bursa mill generally adds 2 to 4 weeks before garment sampling begins.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye negotiate factory contracts or handle customs clearance?
faq.a: No. Itinerary of Türkiye coordinates visits, logistics, scheduling, and independent introductions. All purchase contracts, quality warranties, customs clearance, and export documentation belong to your legal counsel and licensed Turkish customs brokers.

faq.q: Why does flat-fee coordination matter when sourcing in Türkiye?
faq.a: Commission-based sourcing agents often steer buyers toward factories paying the highest referral percentage rather than the best technical fit. Our client-paid flat fee keeps supplier comparisons transparent and aligned solely with your brief.
